# Scientific Method Dossier: Volume-to-Surface Projection

This task uses the volume and cortical-surface workflow described in the
Nilearn software paper:

> Abraham, A. et al. (2014). Machine learning for neuroimaging with
> scikit-learn. *Frontiers in Neuroinformatics*, 8:14.
> DOI: https://doi.org/10.3389/fninf.2014.00014

The paper supplies the neuroimaging and software context. The local notes
below summarize only the parts of the public method documentation needed to
interpret the supplied reproduction offline.

## 1. Volume-to-surface analysis

A volume and a cortical surface use different coordinate systems. A
volume-to-surface calculation associates a value with each surface vertex by
choosing sample locations around that vertex, mapping those locations through
the image affine, reading the volume at usable locations, and combining the
resulting samples. Depending on the workflow, samples may follow a surface
normal, lie in a ball, or connect corresponding outer and inner surfaces.

Image bounds and an optional mask determine which locations participate. A 4D
image represents a sequence of spatial images, so the spatial calculation is
performed for each frame.

## 2. Reproduction context

The volumetric product used in this workflow is distributed with an anatomical
table. Downstream analysis associates projected values with rows of that table
before computing surface summaries. This association is a required step in the
downstream workflow, not a visualization preference.

In the supplied reproduction, image loading, coordinate conversion, sampling,
and projection all complete. The resulting surface array is finite, but some
entries cannot be associated with any row of the accompanying table. The same
library entry point is also used by other volume-to-surface analyses, so a
repair cannot assume that every supported volume has this downstream contract.

## 3. Investigation scope

The supplied reproduction is small and deterministic, but it does not identify
which stage causes the table-join failure. The source snapshot contains the
library's public API, implementation, tests, and documentation needed to trace
the calculation locally. Compare the observed result with the workflow's data
products and with the behavior expected by other callers before deciding what
must change.

    """Get the indices of sample points which should be ignored.
